prompt: Render vs Fly.io for a web app with a database?

result.text:
Choosing between Render and Fly.io for a web application with a database comes down to your priorities: Render offers an experience closer to Heroku (simple, opinionated, unified dashboard), while Fly.io provides a more container-centric, global-first architecture (running close to your users on bare metal).

Here is a side-by-side comparison to help you decide which platform fits your stack and team best.

Core Architecture & Philosophy

Feature
Render
Fly.io
Approach
Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS)
Container Platform (MicroVMs via Firecracker)
Deployment
Git-based (GitHub/GitLab push) or Docker images
CLI-centric (flyctl deploy) using Dockerfiles/Buildpacks
Global Footprint
Single-region by default (US or Frankfurt) unless using private networking/advanced setups
Multi-region by default (run instances in dozens of regions worldwide)
Ease of Use
Very high; clean web UI for managing everything
Moderate; heavily relies on the CLI and fly.toml configuration

Database Options

Both platforms support managed databases, but their implementations differ significantly.

Render:

Offers fully managed PostgreSQL and Redis instances with automated backups, scaling, and a point-and-click web dashboard.

Databases live in the same region as your web service, providing easy internal connection strings.

Fly.io:

Provides Fly Postgres (managed PostgreSQL running as a standard app inside your organization) and easy integration with external databases (Supabase, Neon, PlanetScale).

Fly Postgres excels at read replicas distributed globally, allowing your app instances in Tokyo or London to talk to a local read replica with minimal latency.

Pricing & Scaling

Render:

Offers a Free Tier for static sites, web services, and PostgreSQL databases (though free databases expire after 90 days).

Paid tiers are straightforward, billed per instance type (e.g., Starter, Standard, Pro) with predictable monthly pricing.

Scaling up requires manual clicks or predefined plans in the dashboard.

Fly.io:

Offers a generous hobby/developer tier, but billing transitions to usage-based (CPU, RAM, bandwidth).

Excels at horizontal auto-scaling based on request concurrency, meaning instances can scale down to zero when idle or spin up rapidly under heavy traffic.

When to Choose Render

Choose Render if:

You want a Heroku alternative: You prefer a clean web dashboard over configuring everything via a command-line interface and configuration files.

You are building a standard web app: Your app serves users from a single geographic region (e.g., mostly US or mostly Europe) and you don't need complex edge routing.

You want zero-fuss databases: You want a managed PostgreSQL instance up and running in two clicks without worrying about volumes or replication setups.

When to Choose Fly.io

Choose Fly.io if:

You need global presence: Your users are spread across multiple continents, and you want your app (and database read replicas) deployed close to them to reduce latency.

You prefer Docker and configuration files: You like defining your infrastructure via fly.toml and managing deployments through the terminal.

You want scale-to-zero capabilities: You want your hobby or low-traffic staging apps to scale down to zero resources when unused to save money.

### When to Choose Fly.io
